# Model reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run build:schema` from src/schema/docs.js and the rule base. Do not edit by hand. -->

Rule base 1.0.0. For how to write a model, see the [modelling guide](modelling-guide.md).

## Component types

| Type | Drawn as | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user` | external entity | A person who uses the system (customer, employee, administrator). |
| `web_app` | process | A web front end or backend-for-frontend that serves pages to browsers. |
| `api` | process | An API endpoint or gateway that other clients call (e.g. API Gateway, a REST service edge). |
| `service` | process | A long-running backend service or container (e.g. ECS, EKS pod, EC2 app). |
| `function` | process | A serverless function (e.g. AWS Lambda). |
| `database` | data store | A database (e.g. RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB). |
| `object_storage` | data store | File or object storage (e.g. S3, a container registry). |
| `cache` | data store | An in-memory cache (e.g. ElastiCache Redis). |
| `queue` | data store | A message queue or event bus (e.g. SQS, SNS, Kafka). |
| `identity_provider` | process | A sign-in service (e.g. Cognito, Auth0, Okta). |
| `cdn` | process | A content delivery network (e.g. CloudFront). |
| `load_balancer` | process | A load balancer or ingress (e.g. ALB, NLB). |
| `monitoring` | process | Central logging or security monitoring (e.g. CloudTrail + CloudWatch, a SIEM). Add one if you have it. |
| `external_service` | external entity | A third-party system you do not run (payment provider, SaaS, a partner or bank). |

## Component controls (`properties`)

Anything you leave out counts as **missing**. Unknown names produce a warning with a suggested fix.

| Property | Meaning | Checked by rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `publicFacing` | true if it can be reached directly from the internet (public endpoint, public bucket, public IP). | D-01, D-02, I-03, S-01, S-03 |
| `authentication` | How callers prove who they are: none, basic, api_key, token, oauth or mtls. | E-02, S-01, S-03 |
| `authorization` | true if every request is checked against what this caller may access (per object and per function), not just that they are signed in. | E-02 |
| `mfa` | Identity providers only: true if multi-factor authentication is enforced. | S-03 |
| `inputValidation` | true if all input is validated against an allow-list schema before use. | T-02 |
| `logging` | true if security-relevant actions (or, for data stores, data access) are logged centrally. | R-01, R-02 |
| `rateLimited` | true if requests are throttled per client. | D-01 |
| `encryptionAtRest` | Data stores: true if stored data is encrypted (e.g. KMS-managed keys). | I-01 |
| `dataClassification` | The most sensitive data it holds: public, internal, confidential or restricted. | I-01, I-03, R-02 |
| `leastPrivilege` | true if its IAM role or service account has only the permissions it needs. | E-01 |
| `privileged` | true if it runs as root or in a privileged container. | E-03 |
| `dependencyScanning` | true if its build scans third-party dependencies (npm audit, Snyk, Dependabot). | T-03 |
| `redundancy` | Databases, queues and caches: true if deployed across availability zones or replicated. | D-03 |
| `waf` | true if a web application firewall sits in front of it. | D-02 |

## Data flow fields

| Field | Meaning | Checked by rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Unique id for this data flow, e.g. "f1". | – |
| `from` | Id of the component that sends the data. | – |
| `to` | Id of the component that receives the data. | – |
| `protocol` | e.g. https, tls, grpc, grpcs, tcp, sftp, mllp. https, tls, grpcs, mtls, wss and sftp count as encrypted. | I-02, T-01 |
| `encrypted` | Override whether the channel is encrypted. Leave it out to derive it from the protocol. | I-02, T-01 |
| `authenticated` | true if the receiver authenticates the sender on this flow. Defaults to false. | S-02 |
| `dataClassification` | Most sensitive data on this flow: public, internal, confidential or restricted. Defaults to internal. | I-02 |
| `description` | Optional note shown in tooltips and reports. | – |

## Data classification

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `public` | Meant to be public (marketing pages, product images). |
| `internal` | Not public, but low harm if leaked (internal ids, configuration). |
| `confidential` | Harmful if leaked (orders, customer contact details, business data). |
| `restricted` | Severe harm if leaked: credentials, payment data, health data, government ids. |

## Rules

| Rule | STRIDE category | Applies to | Threat |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S-01 | Spoofing | component | Unauthenticated internet-facing entry point |
| S-02 | Spoofing | data flow | Unauthenticated cross-boundary service call |
| S-03 | Spoofing | component | Weak authentication on exposed component |
| T-01 | Tampering | data flow | Unencrypted data flow across trust boundary |
| T-02 | Tampering | component | Missing input validation |
| T-03 | Tampering | component | Unscanned third-party dependencies |
| R-01 | Repudiation | component | No audit logging on application component |
| R-02 | Repudiation | component | No access logging on sensitive data store |
| R-03 | Repudiation | system | No centralised security monitoring |
| I-01 | Information Disclosure | component | Sensitive data store not encrypted at rest |
| I-02 | Information Disclosure | data flow | Sensitive data transmitted in cleartext |
| I-03 | Information Disclosure | component | Non-public data store exposed to the internet |
| D-01 | Denial of Service | component | No rate limiting on exposed component |
| D-02 | Denial of Service | system | No edge protection for internet-facing system |
| D-03 | Denial of Service | component | Single point of failure in stateful component |
| E-01 | Elevation of Privilege | component | Over-permissive execution role |
| E-02 | Elevation of Privilege | component | Authentication without authorisation |
| E-03 | Elevation of Privilege | component | Component runs with elevated privileges |
